description:
Goal
Apply the same methodology used for the quicksort/operator-sugar non-convergence fix to fixtures2/behavior/enum_take_drop_split.fz, which currently still takes roughly 0.8s and exhibits the same class of excess semantic job churn. The outcome should be an upstream data-model fix or a precise proof that an existing upstream fix already covers it; do not optimize native/codegen or transport symptoms until the earliest incorrect semantic/type fact is identified.

Method
- Run the fixture with --log-telemetry before changing code and reduce the log to the first moving facts, not just the hottest downstream job. Track AnalyzeActivation, ActivationInputs, ReturnType, CallSiteSummary, activation key creation, and any transport/native symptoms only as consumers.
- Identify the earliest point where the data model is wrong: evidence descending, equivalent Ty representatives dirtying revisions, recursive keys splitting equivalent list/tuple/callable surfaces, or callsite summaries preserving decisions that should have been joined upstream.
- Ensure decisions flow downhill. If semantic/type/keying owns the decision, fix it there; artifact, transport, native, and codegen must consume settled facts rather than reconstruct or deduplicate them.
- Add focused tests before or with the fix: one small world/type/semantic regression for the earliest bad model, plus the enum_take_drop_split fixture proof. Prefer telemetry-observed assertions for bounded jobs/revisions where available.
- Update .agent docs with any new invariant. Remove any temporary probes or scaffolding before close.

Starting signal
- Fixture: fixtures2/behavior/enum_take_drop_split.fz.
- Current symptom: about 0.8s compile/run path despite being green; suspected same semantic churn class as the fixed quicksort/operator-sugar issue.
- Useful comparison from prior fix: operator_sugar went from ~55k jobs / 15s timeout to 275 jobs after fixing upstream monotone semantic facts.

Checks
- fz2 --log-telemetry run/interp/build for enum_take_drop_split show bounded job counts and no repeated semantic churn.
- Existing enum_take_drop_split behavior/matrix tests remain green.
- cargo test --lib.
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings if code paths touched are warning-sensitive.

Non-goals
- No local performance patch in transport/native/codegen unless telemetry proves that layer owns the earliest incorrect model.
- No fixture-specific special case for Enum.take/drop/split.

comments.text:
Trace update from minimal Enum.take reducer investigation:

- The original excess-job symptom was upstream: recursive activation keys were splitting on exact tuple/list/callable evidence. The effective fix was to make Types::convergence_class recurse through aggregate structure and collapse callable runtime detail for keying while preserving exact evidence downstream.
- After convergence, the remaining native crash is not a convergence problem. The earliest bad fact observed so far is in transport boundary/source resolution for a first-class reducer input.
- Minimal signal: fn main() { xs = [1,2,3,4,5]; dbg(Enum.take(xs, 3)) } still reaches backend reducer ClosureCall terms with target: None / return_flow: None, then native emits CallClosure direct_target: None and runtime shifts a split reducer return into a one-lane continuation (fz_closure_get_capture_ref idx=1 expected closure ref).
- Artifact/native fixes that reconstruct target identity from local shape are the wrong direction. The authoritative decision should flow from upstream callable-flow / transport boundary facts.
- A useful failing transport assertion shape: for reduce_while_cont/3, inspect the closure-call callee Value position and its callable BoundaryIds. The Ty(0) accumulator activation publishes only BoundaryId(4) on ExecutableInput[2], and that boundary has zero resolutions, while sibling boundaries have resolutions but are not published on this position. That points at missing source-to-boundary resolution for the initial reducer executable input, before artifact/native.
- A separate ABI fact was fixed earlier: direct call argument encoding must consume caller CallArg transport positions, not callee ExecutableInput positions. Another upstream artifact fact was fixed by deduping duplicate FunctionEntry seam facts by lane.

Apply the fz-f98.5 methodology to enum_take_drop_split by first pinning this transport/source-boundary contract with a focused failing test, then tracing why the initial reducer input publication has no source resolutions. Do not make native/codegen choose among callable boundaries.

DE-RISKED INVESTIGATION (f98.6/f98.7 root, HEAD c9baed811 + f98.3). The shared-reduce-bridge failures (f98.6 native multi-boundary, f98.7 reduce/2 EmptyError) are downstream symptoms of OVER-MONOMORPHIZATION of the reducer lambdas.

GROUND TRUTH (Enum.to_list(1..3), transport dump): the to_list reducer fn 173 (#lambda [entry|acc]) has NINE activations -- entry types {Ty0,Ty19,Ty217,Ty220} x acc types {Ty0,Ty37,Ty44} -- all the same source code. The reduce/3 inner lambda fn 174 similarly. These flow through the recursive Enum machinery (reduce_cont/reduce_step/reduce_5) which feeds ascending evidence to the non-recursive reducer at each fixpoint step.

EARLIEST BAD FACT (located): World::canonical_activation_key (world.rs:2926) gates the fz-y6w convergence_collapse on `recursive`: `if !recursive { return key; }`. Non-recursive functions are keyed by PRECISE evidence, so a non-recursive reducer reached through recursive machinery accumulates one activation per evidence vector. The convergence collapse (Ignore-slot -> convergence_class) is exactly what would merge them, but it never runs for non-recursive functions.

THREE FIXES TESTED, each ruled out (this maps the solution space):
1. Native-layer dedup of physically-identical boundaries (derive_callable_entries, the f98.6 attempt): cleared the per-boundary native conflict but the failure MOVED to the interp backend resolver (resolve_backend_callable_executable) -- whack-a-mole; native must not choose (this ticket's own guardrail). REVERTED.
2. Remove the `recursive` gate entirely (blanket collapse, non-recursive too): 10 NEW regressions, ALL capture-surface / suspend-continuation / halt-payload tests (e.g. compiler2_transport_plan_preserves_nested_enum_reduce_predicate_capture_shape). Cause: convergence_class collapses is_pure_callable -> fun_top, erasing the callable surface that IS the boundary identity (fz-f98.3). REVERTED.
3. Surgical: collapse non-recursive non-dispatch DATA slots but PRESERVE callable-carrying slots (added Types::contains_callable; force DispatchDemand::Whole on callable-carrying slots in the non-recursive path). Dropped 10 -> 1 regression (only enum_sort_stable_order_with_custom_comparator) BUT still did NOT fully fix to_list -- fn 174 still fragments into 2 native boundaries. REVERTED.

CONCLUSION: over-monomorphization is MULTI-HEADED, not one keying tweak. The convergence fix must (a) collapse non-recursive non-dispatch data slots WITHOUT collapsing callable surfaces (#3 is the right shape and 90% there), AND (b) handle the residual fn-174 fragmentation + the sort-comparator case -- likely fixpoint-transient bottom activations (Ty0 evidence creating phantom siblings, [[unknown-is-not-none]]) and/or how recursive callers propagate ascending evidence to non-recursive callees. The contains_callable predicate + the non-recursive collapse path from attempt #3 are the starting point; the 10 capture tests + enum_sort + the to_list/reduce2 fixtures are the guardrail set. NO code landed (all three reverted; tree clean at f98.3 commit). f98.6 + f98.7 remain blocked on this.

FULL MECHANISM MAP (Enum.to_list(1..3), reducer fn 173 #lambda [entry|acc], 9 activations). Resolved the Ty identities and found TWO entangled mechanisms -- this is why no single keying change converges:

Ty identities: Ty0=any, Ty19=int, Ty37=[], Ty44=a1 (addr var), Ty219=int|float, Ty220=a0 (addr var), Ty277=the reducer arrow. The 9 reducer activations are entry x acc over {any,int,int|float,a0} x {any,[],a1}.

MECHANISM 1 -- value-template phantoms reach transport. Activations with a0/a1 slots ([a0,a1],[int,a1],[a0,[]]) are value templates (is_value_template). phantom_resolution_keys (runtime_demand.rs:2255) WOULD prune them (ground sibling [int,[]] subsumes), BUT line 458 only does first_class_edges.retain(...) -- it prunes first-class DEMAND EDGES only, NOT direct_edges and NOT the latent EXECUTABLES created during AnalyzeActivation. So template activations survive as executables into the transport plan and fragment boundaries. Gap: phantom pruning is not lifted to the executable/transport level for this path.

MECHANISM 2 -- non-convergent ground evidence. Even pruning templates leaves MULTIPLE ground activations differing by entry type: any (transient top, fixpoint-early), int (settled), int|float (widened union -- Range machinery generalizes element type). convergence_class collapses aggregates (list/tuple) only, NOT scalars/unions, so any vs int vs int|float never merge into one reducer activation. This is the fixpoint-evidence convergence axis ([[unknown-is-not-none]]: 'any' transient should not be a distinct settled activation from 'int').

Attempt #3 (surgical data-slot collapse preserving callables, 10->1 regression) addressed neither mechanism cleanly -- it widened acc lists but left the scalar-entry proliferation (mech 2) and didn't touch the executable-phantom gap (mech 1), and still regressed enum_sort.

CONCLUSION: f98.5 must be decomposed into TWO sub-fixes, each gated on the full guardrail suite:
(5a) Lift value-template phantom pruning to the executable/transport level (not just first_class demand edges) -- a ground-sibling-subsumed template activation must not become a backend executable (fz-hwn.23/27.8 grounding).
(5b) Converge transient/widened scalar evidence for non-recursive callees reached through recursive machinery: 'any' and 'int|float' reducer activations must converge with the settled 'int' one rather than persist as distinct keys.
Neither is landable blind (3 attempts reverted, each broke capture-surface or sort tests). Guardrail set: the 10 capture/continuation tests + enum_sort_stable_order_with_custom_comparator + to_list/reduce2 fixtures. NO code landed; tree clean at f98.3 commit c9baed811.

title: Apply telemetry-first convergence audit to enum_take_drop_split
